-------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m6p3t5 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Banks, Slots, LeaseLen, MaxClock, Admin

NONE == "none"

VARIABLES holdings, deadline, clock, pending, overrides
vars == <<holdings, deadline, clock, pending, overrides>>

HolderOf(s) == { b \in Banks : s \in holdings[b] }

Init ==
    /\ holdings = [b \in Banks |-> {}]
    /\ deadline = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ overrides = 0

\* A bank files a settlement-window request into the shared pending pool.
Request(b, s) ==
    /\ <<b, s>> \notin pending
    /\ pending' = pending \cup { <<b, s>> }
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holdings, deadline, clock, overrides>>

\* A pending request is granted only if the slot is currently free.
Acquire(b, s) ==
    /\ <<b, s>> \in pending
    /\ HolderOf(s) = {}
    /\ holdings' = [holdings EXCEPT ![b] = @ \cup {s}]
    /\ deadline' = [deadline EXCEPT ![s] = clock + LeaseLen]
    /\ pending' = pending \ { <<b, s>> }
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, overrides>>

\* The holder refreshes its lease before it lapses.
Renew(b, s) ==
    /\ s \in holdings[b]
    /\ clock < deadline[s]
    /\ deadline' = [deadline EXCEPT ![s] = clock + LeaseLen]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holdings, clock, pending, overrides>>

\* An expired lease is reclaimed, freeing the slot.
Expire(s) ==
    /\ HolderOf(s) # {}
    /\ clock >= deadline[s]
    /\ holdings' = [b \in Banks |-> holdings[b] \ {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<deadline, clock, pending, overrides>>

\* Admin override: force slot s to bank b, evicting any current holder first.
AdminReassign(b, s) ==
    /\ overrides < MaxClock
    /\ holdings' = [c \in Banks |-> IF c = b THEN holdings[c] \cup {s}
                                            ELSE holdings[c] \ {s}]
    /\ deadline' = [deadline EXCEPT ![s] = clock + LeaseLen]
    /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, pending>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holdings, deadline, pending, overrides>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Banks, s \in Slots : Request(b, s)
    \/ \E b \in Banks, s \in Slots : Acquire(b, s)
    \/ \E b \in Banks, s \in Slots : Renew(b, s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Expire(s)
    \/ \E b \in Banks, s \in Slots : AdminReassign(b, s)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No slot is ever leased to two different banks at the same time.
NoDoubleLease ==
    \A b1, b2 \in Banks :
        b1 # b2 => holdings[b1] \cap holdings[b2] = {}

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Banks = {b1, b2}
    Slots = {s1, s2}
    LeaseLen = 2
    MaxClock = 3
    Admin = adm
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleLease
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch divides the trading day into a handful of
settlement slots, and each participating bank must lease a slot before it can
push its batch through. Banks file requests for the slots they want into a
shared pending pool. A request is granted only when the target slot is
currently free, at which point the winning bank holds a lease that runs until
a fixed expiry time on the settlement clock. A holder may renew its lease
before it lapses to keep the slot for another interval. Once a lease passes
its expiry the slot is reclaimed and returned to the free pool. A privileged
settlement administrator can override the ordinary flow and force a slot to a
specific bank, but doing so first evicts whichever bank currently holds that
slot so the books stay consistent. The clock advances step by step up to the
close of the batch window.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No settlement slot is ever leased to two different banks at
the same time.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m7p6t5 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Students, Courses, Authorized, Admin, MaxVer

NONE == "none"

VARIABLES version, owner, committed, forced, denied
vars == <<version, owner, committed, forced, denied>>

Init ==
    /\ version = [c \in Courses |-> 0]
    /\ owner = [c \in Courses |-> NONE]
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ forced = 0
    /\ denied = 0

\* Compare-and-swap enroll: the student names the version v it read. The swap
\* commits only if the student is authorized and its read is still live (v is
\* the current version), which is the CAS success condition.
Enroll(st, c, v) ==
    /\ st \in Authorized
    /\ v = version[c]
    /\ version[c] < MaxVer
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![c] = st]
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![c] = @ + 1]
    /\ committed' = committed \cup { [student |-> st, course |-> c, ver |-> v] }
    /\ UNCHANGED <<forced, denied>>

\* An attempt that is unauthorized or stale is rejected and never commits.
Reject(st, c, v) ==
    /\ st \notin Authorized \/ v # version[c]
    /\ denied < MaxVer + 1
    /\ denied' = denied + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, owner, committed, forced>>

\* Admin override hand-places an authorized student and bumps the version,
\* invalidating any concurrent reads.
AdminPlace(st, c) ==
    /\ st \in Authorized
    /\ forced < MaxVer
    /\ version[c] < MaxVer
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![c] = st]
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![c] = @ + 1]
    /\ committed' = committed \cup { [student |-> st, course |-> c, ver |-> version[c]] }
    /\ forced' = forced + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED denied

Quiesce ==
    /\ \A c \in Courses : version[c] = MaxVer
    /\ denied = MaxVer + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E st \in Students, c \in Courses, v \in 0..MaxVer : Enroll(st, c, v)
    \/ \E st \in Students, c \in Courses, v \in 0..MaxVer : Reject(st, c, v)
    \/ \E st \in Students, c \in Courses : AdminPlace(st, c)
    \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every committed enrollment was written by a student on the authorized roster.
CommitsAuthorized ==
    /\ \A r \in committed : r.student \in Authorized
    /\ \A c \in Courses : owner[c] = NONE \/ owner[c] \in Authorized

=============================================================================
nl:
A university course-registration system guards each course seat with a shared
version register, and students enroll through a compare-and-swap protocol.
A student first reads the current version of the course it wants. It may then
attempt to commit an enrollment, but the swap succeeds only if two things hold:
the student is on the authorized roster, and the version it read still matches
the live version, meaning no one else has changed the seat in the meantime.
A read that has fallen behind the live version is stale and gets discarded so
the student must retry. The registrar holds a privileged admin override that
can hand-place an authorized student directly, and doing so bumps the version
so that any outstanding reads become stale. Unauthorized users and students
acting on stale reads are never allowed to commit.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every committed course enrollment was written by a student on
the authorized roster.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od19m5p6t2 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Books, Librarians, Authorized, Instances, Quorum

NONE == "none"

VARIABLES reservedBy, pledged, voterSnap, denied
vars == <<reservedBy, pledged, voterSnap, denied>>

Init ==
    /\ reservedBy = [b \in Books |-> NONE]
    /\ pledged = [b \in Books |-> {}]
    /\ voterSnap = [b \in Books |-> {}]
    /\ denied = 0

\* An authorized librarian pledges a vote toward reserving book b.
Pledge(l, b) ==
    /\ l \in Authorized
    /\ l \notin pledged[b]
    /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![b] = @ \cup {l}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reservedBy, voterSnap, denied>>

\* A librarian withdraws a pending pledge before the vote closes.
Withdraw(l, b) ==
    /\ l \in pledged[b]
    /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![b] = @ \ {l}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reservedBy, voterSnap, denied>>

\* Either shared branch grants the reservation once a quorum has pledged and
\* the book is free in the common pool. The winning quorum is snapshotted.
Grant(b, i) ==
    /\ reservedBy[b] = NONE
    /\ Cardinality(pledged[b]) >= Quorum
    /\ reservedBy' = [reservedBy EXCEPT ![b] = i]
    /\ voterSnap' = [voterSnap EXCEPT ![b] = pledged[b]]
    /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED denied

\* A quorum that cannot be assembled from unauthorized pledgers is rejected.
RejectUnauthorized(l, b) ==
    /\ l \notin Authorized
    /\ denied < Quorum + 1
    /\ denied' = denied + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reservedBy, pledged, voterSnap>>

\* The book is returned to the shared pool for another branch to reserve.
Release(b) ==
    /\ reservedBy[b] # NONE
    /\ reservedBy' = [reservedBy EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
    /\ voterSnap' = [voterSnap EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pledged, denied>>

Next ==
    \/ \E l \in Librarians, b \in Books : Pledge(l, b)
    \/ \E l \in Librarians, b \in Books : Withdraw(l, b)
    \/ \E b \in Books, i \in Instances : Grant(b, i)
    \/ \E l \in Librarians, b \in Books : RejectUnauthorized(l, b)
    \/ \E b \in Books : Release(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every active reservation is backed by a quorum drawn only from authorized
\* librarians -- no unauthorized or under-quorum party ever forces a hold.
ReservationsQuorate ==
    \A b \in Books :
        reservedBy[b] = NONE
            \/ ( Cardinality(voterSnap[b]) >= Quorum
                 /\ voterSnap[b] \subseteq Authorized )

=============================================================================
nl:
A library book reservation system runs across two independent branch instances
that share one common pool of books. Reserving any book is not a unilateral act:
it requires quorum voting by the branch's librarians. An authorized librarian
pledges a vote toward reserving a particular book, and may withdraw that pledge
before the vote closes. Either branch may grant the reservation once a quorum of
pledges has accumulated and the book is still free in the shared pool, and the
identity of the approving quorum is recorded with the hold. Pledges from anyone
not on the authorized librarian list are rejected outright and can never count
toward a quorum. A reserved book is eventually released back into the shared
pool so the other branch can compete for it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every active reservation is backed by a quorum drawn entirely
from authorized librarians.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m5p0t4 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Trains, Blocks, Controllers, Quorum

NONE == "none"

VARIABLES pos, approvals, inService
vars == <<pos, approvals, inService>>

Init ==
    /\ pos = [t \in Trains |-> NONE]
    /\ approvals = [t \in Trains |-> {}]
    /\ inService = Blocks

\* A signal controller approves a train's request to occupy the next block.
Approve(ct, t) ==
    /\ ct \notin approvals[t]
    /\ pos[t] = NONE
    /\ approvals' = [approvals EXCEPT ![t] = @ \cup {ct}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pos, inService>>

\* The train enters block b only after a quorum of controllers approves, the
\* block is in service, and no other train currently holds it.
Enter(t, b) ==
    /\ pos[t] = NONE
    /\ b \in inService
    /\ Cardinality(approvals[t]) >= Quorum
    /\ \A u \in Trains : pos[u] # b
    /\ pos' = [pos EXCEPT ![t] = b]
    /\ approvals' = [approvals EXCEPT ![t] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED inService

\* The train clears the block, releasing it for the next mover.
Leave(t) ==
    /\ pos[t] # NONE
    /\ pos' = [pos EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<approvals, inService>>

\* A block is taken out of service for maintenance (runtime capacity shrink),
\* but only while it is unoccupied.
CloseBlock(b) ==
    /\ b \in inService
    /\ \A u \in Trains : pos[u] # b
    /\ inService' = inService \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pos, approvals>>

\* A block is returned to service (runtime capacity grow).
OpenBlock(b) ==
    /\ b \notin inService
    /\ inService' = inService \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pos, approvals>>

Next ==
    \/ \E ct \in Controllers, t \in Trains : Approve(ct, t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : Enter(t, b)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Leave(t)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : CloseBlock(b)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : OpenBlock(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No two distinct trains ever occupy the same track block at once.
BlockExclusive ==
    \A t1, t2 \in Trains :
        (t1 # t2 /\ pos[t1] # NONE) => pos[t1] # pos[t2]

=============================================================================
nl:
A subway signalling block system divides the track into fixed blocks, and each
block is a critical resource that at most one train may occupy. Before a train
may enter the next block, a quorum of independent signal controllers must
approve its request; a single controller's nod is never enough. Once a quorum
has approved and the target block is both in service and unoccupied, the train
moves in and its pending approvals are cleared. A train later clears the block,
releasing it for the next mover. Operations may take a block out of service for
maintenance, shrinking capacity at runtime, but only while that block is empty;
a maintained block can be returned to service later. Capacity therefore changes
while trains keep running.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct trains ever occupy the same track block at the
same time.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m5p5t3 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Devices, Authorized, Quorum, MaxClock

VARIABLES sealed, sealVoters, pledged, clock
vars == <<sealed, sealVoters, pledged, clock>>

Init ==
    /\ sealed = FALSE
    /\ sealVoters = {}
    /\ pledged = {}
    /\ clock = 0

\* An authorized lock device casts (a possibly slow) vote to permanently seal
\* the network. Slowness is fine -- votes simply accrue over time.
Pledge(d) ==
    /\ d \in Authorized
    /\ d \notin pledged
    /\ pledged' = pledged \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sealed, sealVoters, clock>>

\* A device rescinds its pending vote before the seal fires.
Rescind(d) ==
    /\ d \in pledged
    /\ pledged' = pledged \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sealed, sealVoters, clock>>

\* The irreversible seal fires at most once, and only after a quorum has voted.
Seal ==
    /\ ~sealed
    /\ Cardinality(pledged) >= Quorum
    /\ sealed' = TRUE
    /\ sealVoters' = pledged
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pledged, clock>>

\* Time advances; slow devices are still permitted to vote afterward.
Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sealed, sealVoters, pledged>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Devices : Pledge(d)
    \/ \E d \in Devices : Rescind(d)
    \/ Seal
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* If the network was ever permanently sealed, the sealing decision carried a
\* quorum drawn entirely from authorized devices.
SealAuthorized ==
    sealed => ( Cardinality(sealVoters) >= Quorum /\ sealVoters \subseteq Authorized )

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Devices = {d1, d2, d3}
    Authorized = {d1, d2}
    Quorum = 2
    MaxClock = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SealAuthorized
nl:
A smart-home door lock network can be permanently sealed, an irreversible step
that locks the home into a hardened state and can never be undone. Because the
step is so consequential, it requires quorum voting among the network's lock
devices rather than a single command. An authorized device casts a vote toward
sealing; devices may be slow to respond but are assumed not to fail, so votes
simply accrue over time, and a device may rescind its pending vote before the
seal fires. Once a quorum of votes has gathered, the seal fires exactly once and
records the quorum that authorized it; no further seal can occur afterward.
Votes from devices that are not authorized never count. Time may pass while the
network waits for slow devices to weigh in.

SAFETY PROPERTY: If the network is ever permanently sealed, that irreversible
seal was authorized by a quorum of authorized devices.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m7p4t5 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Traders, Cap, MaxVer, Admin

VARIABLES filled, version, granted, overrides, denied
vars == <<filled, version, granted, overrides, denied>>

Qtys == {1, 2}

Init ==
    /\ filled = 0
    /\ version = 0
    /\ granted = [t \in Traders |-> 0]
    /\ overrides = 0
    /\ denied = 0

\* Compare-and-swap order fill: the trader names the register version v it read.
\* The fill commits only if the read is live and capacity is not exceeded.
Submit(t, q, v) ==
    /\ v = version
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ filled + q <= Cap
    /\ filled' = filled + q
    /\ granted' = [granted EXCEPT ![t] = @ + q]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<overrides, denied>>

\* A stale order (its read no longer matches the live version) is rejected.
RejectStale(v) ==
    /\ v # version
    /\ denied < MaxVer + 1
    /\ denied' = denied + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<filled, version, granted, overrides>>

\* A trader cancels part of its fill, returning shares to the auction book.
Cancel(t, q) ==
    /\ q \in Qtys
    /\ granted[t] >= q
    /\ filled' = filled - q
    /\ granted' = [granted EXCEPT ![t] = @ - q]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, overrides, denied>>

\* Admin override: the exchange hand-allocates shares, still capped by supply.
AdminAllocate(t, q) ==
    /\ q \in Qtys
    /\ overrides < MaxVer
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ filled + q <= Cap
    /\ filled' = filled + q
    /\ granted' = [granted EXCEPT ![t] = @ + q]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED denied

Quiesce ==
    /\ version = MaxVer
    /\ \A t \in Traders : granted[t] = 0
    /\ denied = MaxVer + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Traders, q \in Qtys, v \in 0..MaxVer : Submit(t, q, v)
    \/ \E v \in 0..MaxVer : RejectStale(v)
    \/ \E t \in Traders, q \in Qtys : Cancel(t, q)
    \/ \E t \in Traders, q \in Qtys : AdminAllocate(t, q)
    \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The total shares allocated in the opening auction never exceed the supply cap.
CapacityRespected == filled <= Cap

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Traders = {t1, t2}
    Cap = 3
    MaxVer = 3
    Admin = ex
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityRespected
nl:
A stock exchange opening auction fills orders against a fixed supply of shares,
coordinated through a shared compare-and-swap register that carries a version
number. A trader reads the current version, then submits an order naming the
version it saw; the fill commits only if that read is still live (the version
has not moved) and the requested quantity keeps the total filled within the
supply cap. An order whose read has gone stale is rejected and must be retried.
A trader may cancel part of its fill, returning those shares to the book. The
exchange holds a privileged admin override that can hand-allocate shares
directly, but it too is bounded by the available supply. Every successful fill
or override advances the register version so concurrent stale reads are caught.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of shares allocated in the opening auction
never exceeds the fixed supply cap.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m4p6t1 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Users, Authorized, JobIds, MaxQueue, MaxDenied

Pairs == Users \X JobIds

VARIABLES queue, epoch, denied, printed
vars == <<queue, epoch, denied, printed>>

Init ==
    /\ queue = {}
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ denied = 0
    /\ printed = 0

\* An authorized user submits a job stamped with the version v it read. The
\* spool accepts it only if the read is live and the bounded queue has room
\* (backpressure). Jobs are held as a set, so they may be served in any order.
Submit(u, id, v) ==
    /\ u \in Authorized
    /\ v = epoch
    /\ Cardinality(queue) < MaxQueue
    /\ <<u, id>> \notin queue
    /\ queue' = queue \cup { <<u, id>> }
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, denied, printed>>

\* An unauthorized submission, or one carrying a stale version, is rejected.
Reject(u, v) ==
    /\ (u \notin Authorized \/ v # epoch)
    /\ denied < MaxDenied
    /\ denied' = denied + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, epoch, printed>>

\* The printer pulls an arbitrary queued job (reordering is allowed) and prints.
Print(j) ==
    /\ j \in queue
    /\ printed < MaxDenied
    /\ queue' = queue \ {j}
    /\ printed' = printed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, denied>>

\* An admin reconfiguration bumps the spool epoch, invalidating in-flight jobs.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxDenied
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, denied, printed>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ epoch = MaxDenied
    /\ denied = MaxDenied
    /\ printed = MaxDenied
    /\ Cardinality(queue) = MaxQueue
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E u \in Users, id \in JobIds, v \in 0..MaxDenied : Submit(u, id, v)
    \/ \E u \in Users, v \in 0..MaxDenied : Reject(u, v)
    \/ \E j \in Pairs : Print(j)
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every job sitting in the spool queue was submitted by an authorized user.
QueueAuthorized == \A j \in queue : j[1] \in Authorized

=============================================================================
nl:
A print shop job spooler accepts jobs from many users into a bounded work queue
and streams them to the printer. The queue has a fixed capacity, so when it is
full the spool exerts backpressure and refuses new submissions until room opens.
Each submission is stamped with the spool epoch the user read; the spool accepts
a job only if the submitter is on the authorized user list and the stamped epoch
is still current, so both unauthorized users and users acting on a stale epoch
are turned away. Because the printer is free to pull whichever queued job it
likes next, jobs may be served in a different order than submitted -- messages
can be reordered. An administrator may reconfigure the spool, bumping the epoch
and invalidating any jobs still carrying the old one.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every job resident in the spool queue was submitted by a user
on the authorized list.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m1p5t4 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS N, MaxSeats

VARIABLES token, cap, seated, permit, sealed
vars == <<token, cap, seated, permit, sealed>>

Nodes == 0 .. N - 1
RingNext(x) == (x + 1) % N

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ cap = MaxSeats
    /\ seated = 0
    /\ permit = 1        \* the single one-time finalization capability
    /\ sealed = 0        \* count of finalizations that have occurred

\* The exclusive-access token advances one step around the registration ring.
PassToken ==
    /\ token' = RingNext(token)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, seated, permit, sealed>>

\* Only the current token holder may seat a student, and only within capacity.
Enroll(n) ==
    /\ token = n
    /\ seated < cap
    /\ seated' = seated + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, cap, permit, sealed>>

\* Capacity is adjusted at runtime, but never below the students already seated.
Resize(k) ==
    /\ k \in 0 .. MaxSeats
    /\ k >= seated
    /\ cap' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, seated, permit, sealed>>

\* The irreversible finalization consumes the one-time permit exactly once; the
\* token holder locks the roster and the permit is spent forever.
Finalize(n) ==
    /\ token = n
    /\ permit >= 1
    /\ permit' = permit - 1
    /\ sealed' = sealed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, cap, seated>>

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Enroll(n)
    \/ \E k \in 0 .. MaxSeats : Resize(k)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Finalize(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The one-time finalization permit and the finalizations performed always sum
\* to one: the irreversible roster lock can happen at most once, never twice.
FinalizeOnce == permit + sealed = 1

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    N = 3
    MaxSeats = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT FinalizeOnce
nl:
A university course-registration system coordinates several registration nodes
with a token ring: a single token circulates around the ring, and only the node
currently holding the token may act, which grants exclusive access. The token
advances one step at a time around the ring. The holder may seat a student as
long as the section is under its seat capacity, and that capacity can be resized
at runtime by the registrar, though never below the number of students already
seated. Finalizing the roster is an irreversible act: it consumes a single
one-time permit, locking the section permanently, and once spent the permit can
never authorize a second finalization. The system therefore guarantees the
roster is finalized at most once across the whole ring.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The irreversible roster finalization happens at most once.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m6p4t3 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Flights, Runways, Cap, LeaseLen, MaxClock

NONE == "none"

VARIABLES owner, deadline, clock, held
vars == <<owner, deadline, clock, held>>

Init ==
    /\ owner = [r \in Runways |-> NONE]
    /\ deadline = [r \in Runways |-> 0]
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ held = 0

\* A flight acquires a free runway, but only if the concurrent-approach cap has
\* not been reached. The lease runs until a fixed expiry on the tower clock.
Acquire(f, r) ==
    /\ owner[r] = NONE
    /\ held < Cap
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![r] = f]
    /\ deadline' = [deadline EXCEPT ![r] = clock + LeaseLen]
    /\ held' = held + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

\* The holding flight refreshes its lease before it lapses.
Renew(f, r) ==
    /\ owner[r] = f
    /\ clock < deadline[r]
    /\ deadline' = [deadline EXCEPT ![r] = clock + LeaseLen]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, clock, held>>

\* A lapsed lease is reclaimed by the tower, freeing the runway.
Expire(r) ==
    /\ owner[r] # NONE
    /\ clock >= deadline[r]
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
    /\ held' = held - 1

    /\ held' = held - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<deadline, clock>>

    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, deadline, held>>

    \/ \E f \in Flights, r \in Runways : Acquire(f, r)
    \/ \E f \in Flights, r \in Runways : Renew(f, r)
    \/ \E r \in Runways : Expire(r)
    \/ \E f \in Flights, r \in Runways : Release(f, r)

been reached, and the lease then runs until a fixed expiry on the tower clock.

assumed not to have failed, so it will eventually release its runway; and if a
lease lapses before then, the tower reclaims it automatically. Both voluntary
release and automatic expiry return the runway to the free pool and free a slot
under the cap. The clock advances step by step.

the concurrent-approach capacity cap.

CONSTANTS Drones, Cells, Total

NONE == "none"

VARIABLES coarse, fine, fuel, depot
vars == <<coarse, fine, fuel, depot>>

RECURSIVE SumFuel(_)
SumFuel(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET d == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN fuel[d] + SumFuel(S \ {d})

Init ==
    /\ coarse = NONE                       \* coarse region lock (whole swarm)
    /\ fine = [c \in Cells |-> NONE]        \* fine per-cell locks
    /\ fuel = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ depot = Total

\* A drone takes the coarse region lock (must be acquired before any fine lock).
LockCoarse(d) ==
    /\ coarse = NONE
    /\ coarse' = d
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, fuel, depot>>

\* Holding the coarse lock, a drone takes the fine lock on a survey cell.
LockFine(d, c) ==
    /\ coarse = d
    /\ fine[c] = NONE
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![c] = d]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fuel, depot>>

\* A drone holding both locks draws one unit of fuel from the shared depot.
\* Requests arrive in any order; conservation must hold regardless.
Draw(d, c) ==
    /\ coarse = d
    /\ fine[c] = d
    /\ depot > 0
    /\ depot' = depot - 1
    /\ fuel' = [fuel EXCEPT ![d] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine>>

\* A drone returns a unit of fuel to the depot.
Return(d) ==
    /\ fuel[d] > 0
    /\ fuel' = [fuel EXCEPT ![d] = @ - 1]
    /\ depot' = depot + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine>>

\* A drone drops all its locks, coarse and fine.
Unlock(d) ==
    /\ (coarse = d \/ \E c \in Cells : fine[c] = d)
    /\ coarse' = IF coarse = d THEN NONE ELSE coarse
    /\ fine' = [c \in Cells |-> IF fine[c] = d THEN NONE ELSE fine[c]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fuel, depot>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones : LockCoarse(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones, c \in Cells : LockFine(d, c)
    \/ \E d \in Drones, c \in Cells : Draw(d, c)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Return(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Unlock(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Total fuel is conserved: the depot plus all drone reserves always equals the
\* fixed initial supply -- nothing is created or destroyed.
FuelConserved == depot + SumFuel(Drones) = Total

depot. To coordinate access the swarm uses hierarchical locking: a drone must
first take a coarse region lock covering the whole survey area, and only while
holding it may it take a fine lock on an individual survey cell. A drone that
holds both the coarse lock and the fine lock on a cell may draw one unit of fuel
from the depot into its own reserve, and it may later return fuel to the depot.

model imposes no ordering on them. A drone can drop all of its locks at once.
Throughout all of this the fuel is only ever moved between the depot and drone
reserves, never minted or lost.

equals the fixed initial supply.

specific hall call it wants. A car may assign itself a call only when it holds
both locks and no other car is already serving that call. When the car finishes,

be slow rather than failed, so a dispatch clock advances while cars work and a

keeps the assignment step race-free.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m9p1t0 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Nodes, MaxOps

NONE == "none"

VARIABLES record, epoch, applied, snap, crashed
vars == <<record, epoch, applied, snap, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ record = 0                        \* the shared page-count record
    /\ epoch = 0                         \* current reconfiguration epoch
    /\ applied = 0                       \* number of updates that have committed
    /\ snap = [n \in Nodes |-> [valid |-> FALSE, e |-> 0, v |-> 0]]
    /\ crashed = {}

\* A live node reads the shared record together with the current epoch.
Read(n) ==
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ ~snap[n].valid
    /\ epoch < MaxOps
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![n] = [valid |-> TRUE, e |-> epoch, v |-> record]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, epoch, applied, crashed>>

\* Commit a read-modify-write, but only if the read is still on the live epoch
\* (optimistic-lock success). This prevents one update from clobbering another.
Commit(n) ==
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ snap[n].valid
    /\ snap[n].e = epoch
    /\ record' = snap[n].v + 1
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ applied' = applied + 1
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![n] = [valid |-> FALSE, e |-> 0, v |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

\* A read that has fallen behind the live epoch is discarded, forcing a retry.
Retry(n) ==
    /\ snap[n].valid
    /\ snap[n].e # epoch
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![n] = [valid |-> FALSE, e |-> 0, v |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, epoch, applied, crashed>>

\* An operator reconfiguration bumps the epoch, invalidating in-flight reads.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxOps
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, applied, snap, crashed>>

\* A single node may crash silently and thereafter take no steps.
Crash(n) ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ crashed' = {n}
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![n] = [valid |-> FALSE, e |-> 0, v |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, epoch, applied>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ epoch = MaxOps
    /\ \A n \in Nodes : ~snap[n].valid
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Read(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Commit(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Retry(n)
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Crash(n)
    \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No committed update is ever lost: the shared record equals the number of
\* updates that have committed, so no writer's increment was overwritten.
NoLostUpdate == record = applied

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {n1, n2}
    MaxOps = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A print shop job spooler keeps a shared page-count record that several worker
nodes update concurrently, coordinated by an epoch-numbered reconfiguration
scheme. A node updates the record with a read-modify-write: it first reads the
record together with the current epoch into a private snapshot, then tries to
commit an incremented value. The commit succeeds only if the snapshot's epoch
still matches the live epoch -- an optimistic lock that guarantees no writer
overwrites another writer's committed increment. A read that has fallen behind
the epoch is discarded and the node retries. An operator may reconfigure the
spool, bumping the epoch and invalidating any in-flight reads. One worker node
may crash silently at any point and then does nothing further; the record must
still reflect every committed update.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No committed update to the shared page-count record is ever
lost or overwritten.

CONSTANTS Robots, Aisles, MaxClock

NONE == "none"

VARIABLES zoneLock, aisleLock, pos, clock
vars == <<zoneLock, aisleLock, pos, clock>>

Init ==
    /\ zoneLock = NONE                        \* coarse warehouse-zone lock
    /\ aisleLock = [a \in Aisles |-> NONE]      \* fine per-aisle lock
    /\ pos = [r \in Robots |-> NONE]
    /\ clock = 0

\* A robot takes the coarse zone lock, a prerequisite for any fine aisle lock.
GrabZone(r) ==
    /\ zoneLock = NONE
    /\ pos[r] = NONE
    /\ zoneLock' = r
    /\ UNCHANGED <<aisleLock, pos, clock>>

\* Holding the zone lock, the robot takes the fine lock on the aisle it wants.
GrabAisle(r, a) ==
    /\ zoneLock = r
    /\ aisleLock[a] = NONE
    /\ aisleLock' = [aisleLock EXCEPT ![a] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, pos, clock>>

\* The robot enters the aisle only if it holds both locks and the aisle is
\* empty, giving it mutually exclusive use of the aisle.
Enter(r, a) ==
    /\ zoneLock = r
    /\ aisleLock[a] = r
    /\ \A q \in Robots : pos[q] # a
    /\ pos' = [pos EXCEPT ![r] = a]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, aisleLock, clock>>

\* The robot leaves the aisle and drops both of its locks.
Leave(r) ==
    /\ pos[r] # NONE
    /\ pos' = [pos EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
    /\ aisleLock' = [a \in Aisles |-> IF aisleLock[a] = r THEN NONE ELSE aisleLock[a]]
    /\ zoneLock' = IF zoneLock = r THEN NONE ELSE zoneLock
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

\* The fleet clock advances; a slow (not failed) robot just takes more ticks.

    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, aisleLock, pos>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots : GrabZone(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, a \in Aisles : GrabAisle(r, a)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, a \in Aisles : Enter(r, a)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Leave(r)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No two distinct robots ever occupy the same aisle at the same time.
AisleExclusive ==
    \A r, q \in Robots :
        (r # q /\ pos[r] # NONE) => pos[r] # pos[q]

    MaxClock = 2

robot at a time, since two robots in the same aisle would collide. Access is
arbitrated by hierarchical locking: a robot first grabs a coarse warehouse-zone
lock, and only while holding it may it grab the fine lock on the particular
aisle it wants to enter. A robot enters an aisle only when it holds both locks
and the aisle is currently empty, which gives it mutually exclusive use of that
aisle. When finished, the robot leaves the aisle and releases both of its locks
so another robot may proceed. A robot may be slow rather than failed, so a fleet
clock advances while robots work and a lagging robot simply needs more ticks.
The coarse-then-fine discipline keeps aisle entry race-free.

time.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m0p3t1 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Buyers, Slots, MaxVer

NONE == "none"

VARIABLES claim, ver, snap, retries
vars == <<claim, ver, snap, retries>>

Init ==
    /\ claim = [b \in Buyers |-> NONE]                 \* slot each buyer holds
    /\ ver = [s \in Slots |-> 0]                        \* optimistic version per slot
    /\ snap = [b \in Buyers |-> [valid |-> FALSE, s |-> NONE, v |-> 0]]
    /\ retries = 0

\* A buyer optimistically reads a slot's version (no lock is taken).
ReadSlot(b, s) ==
    /\ claim[b] = NONE
    /\ ~snap[b].valid
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![b] = [valid |-> TRUE, s |-> s, v |-> ver[s]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<claim, ver, retries>>

\* The buyer commits its reservation only if its read is still current (version
\* unchanged) and the slot is unclaimed. Requests may be handled in any order.
Reserve(b) ==
    /\ snap[b].valid
    /\ ver[snap[b].s] = snap[b].v
    /\ \A q \in Buyers : claim[q] # snap[b].s
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![b] = snap[b].s]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![snap[b].s] = (@ + 1) % (MaxVer + 1)]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![b] = [valid |-> FALSE, s |-> NONE, v |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED retries

\* A read that lost the optimistic race (version moved) is retried.
Retry(b) ==
    /\ snap[b].valid
    /\ ver[snap[b].s] # snap[b].v
    /\ retries < MaxVer
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![b] = [valid |-> FALSE, s |-> NONE, v |-> 0]]
    /\ retries' = retries + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<claim, ver>>

\* The buyer collects its item, releasing the slot back to the machine.
Collect(b) ==
    /\ claim[b] # NONE
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![claim[b]] = (@ + 1) % (MaxVer + 1)]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, retries>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Buyers, s \in Slots : ReadSlot(b, s)
    \/ \E b \in Buyers : Reserve(b)
    \/ \E b \in Buyers : Retry(b)
    \/ \E b \in Buyers : Collect(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No product slot is ever reserved by two different buyers at once.
NoDoubleVend ==
    \A b, q \in Buyers :
        (b # q /\ claim[b] # NONE) => claim[b] # claim[q]

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Buyers = {x, y}
    Slots = {s1, s2}
    MaxVer = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleVend
nl:
A vending machine network lets several buyers reserve product slots concurrently
using optimistic locking with retry. A buyer optimistically reads the version
number of a slot it wants, taking no lock. It then tries to reserve that slot,
but the reservation commits only if the slot's version has not changed since the
read (the optimistic check) and the slot is still unclaimed by anyone. Because
buyer requests can arrive and be serviced in any order, the model imposes no
ordering on them. If the version moved under a buyer -- someone else got there
first -- the read is stale and the buyer simply retries. Once a buyer collects
its item the slot is released and its version bumped for the next round. The
optimistic check ensures two buyers never both win the same slot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No product slot is ever reserved by two different buyers at the
same time.

vars == <<homeLock, hubLock, ledger, snap, committed, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ homeLock = NONE                          \* coarse whole-home lock
    /\ hubLock = NONE                           \* fine lock on the record hub
    /\ ledger = {}                              \* the shared access-record set
    /\ snap = [c \in Controllers |-> [valid |-> FALSE, seen |-> {}]]
    /\ committed = {}                           \* controllers whose entry committed
    /\ crashed = {}

\* A controller takes the coarse home lock (needed before the fine hub lock).
GrabHome(c) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ homeLock = NONE
    /\ homeLock' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hubLock, ledger, snap, committed, crashed>>

\* Holding the home lock, the controller takes the fine record-hub lock.
GrabHub(c) ==
    /\ homeLock = c
    /\ hubLock = NONE
    /\ hubLock' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<homeLock, ledger, snap, committed, crashed>>

\* Under both locks, the controller reads the current ledger into a snapshot.
ReadLedger(c) ==
    /\ homeLock = c
    /\ hubLock = c
    /\ ~snap[c].valid
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = [valid |-> TRUE, seen |-> ledger]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<homeLock, hubLock, ledger, committed, crashed>>

\* The controller writes its own entry back on top of the snapshot it read.
\* Because it holds both locks no one else could have written meanwhile, so no
\* prior entry is lost.
Commit(c) ==
    /\ homeLock = c
    /\ hubLock = c
    /\ snap[c].valid
    /\ ledger' = snap[c].seen \cup {c}
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {c}
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = [valid |-> FALSE, seen |-> {}]]
    /\ homeLock' = NONE
    /\ hubLock' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

\* A controller may crash silently and then takes no further steps; if it held
\* locks they are released so the system makes progress.
Crash(c) ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ c \notin committed
    /\ crashed' = {c}
    /\ homeLock' = IF homeLock = c THEN NONE ELSE homeLock
    /\ hubLock' = IF hubLock = c THEN NONE ELSE hubLock
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = [valid |-> FALSE, seen |-> {}]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, committed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : GrabHome(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : GrabHub(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : ReadLedger(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Commit(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Crash(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No committed access entry is ever lost: every controller that has committed
\* still appears in the shared ledger.
NoLostEntry == committed \subseteq ledger

controllers append to, protected by hierarchical locking. To write, a controller
first grabs a coarse whole-home lock, and only while holding it may it grab the
fine lock on the record hub. Holding both locks, it reads the current ledger
into a private snapshot and then writes its own entry back on top of that
snapshot. Because it holds both locks for the whole read-modify-write, no other
controller could have written in between, so no previously committed entry is
ever dropped. When done it releases both locks. Any single controller may crash
silently and then does nothing further; if it was holding locks they are freed
so others can proceed. The ledger must always retain every entry that has
committed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No committed access entry is ever lost from the shared ledger.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m1p3t2 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Banks, Slots, Instances, MaxPass

NONE == "none"

VARIABLES token, holdings, passes
vars == <<token, holdings, passes>>

Init ==
    /\ token = CHOOSE i \in Instances : TRUE     \* which instance holds the ring token
    /\ holdings = [b \in Banks |-> {}]
    /\ passes = 0

\* The exclusive-access token is handed to the other shared instance.
PassToken(i) ==
    /\ token # i
    /\ passes < MaxPass
    /\ token' = i
    /\ passes' = passes + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED holdings

\* Only the instance currently holding the token may allocate a settlement slot,
\* and only when that slot is free in the shared pool.
Allocate(i, b, s) ==
    /\ token = i
    /\ \A c \in Banks : s \notin holdings[c]
    /\ holdings' = [holdings EXCEPT ![b] = @ \cup {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, passes>>

\* The token-holding instance releases a slot back to the shared pool.
Release(i, b, s) ==
    /\ token = i
    /\ s \in holdings[b]
    /\ holdings' = [holdings EXCEPT ![b] = @ \ {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, passes>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ passes = MaxPass
    /\ \A b \in Banks : holdings[b] = Slots
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : PassToken(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, b \in Banks, s \in Slots : Allocate(i, b, s)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, b \in Banks, s \in Slots : Release(i, b, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No settlement slot is ever allocated to two different banks at the same time.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A a, b \in Banks :
        a # b => holdings[a] \cap holdings[b] = {}

=============================================================================
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch is run jointly by two independent instances
that share one common pool of settlement slots. Exclusive authority to allocate
slots circulates between the instances as a ring token: the token is handed back
and forth, and only the instance currently holding it may act. The token-holding
instance may allocate a settlement slot to a bank, but only when that slot is
still free across the whole shared pool. The holding instance may also release a
slot back to the pool. Because exactly one instance holds the token at a time and
it checks the shared pool before allocating, the two instances can never hand the
same slot to two different banks. Allocation authority passes a bounded number of
times over the batch window.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No settlement slot is ever allocated to two different banks at
the same time.

CONSTANTS Feeders, Windows, MaxVer

VARIABLES holdings, ver, snap, retries
vars == <<holdings, ver, snap, retries>>

    /\ holdings = [f \in Feeders |-> {}]                \* shed windows each feeder holds
    /\ ver = [w \in Windows |-> 0]                       \* optimistic version per window
    /\ snap = [f \in Feeders |-> [valid |-> FALSE, w |-> CHOOSE x \in Windows : TRUE, v |-> 0]]
    /\ retries = 0

    /\ ~snap[f].valid
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![f] = [valid |-> TRUE, w |-> w, v |-> ver[w]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holdings, ver, retries>>

\* already holds it. Concurrent claim requests may be processed in any order.

    /\ snap[f].valid
    /\ ver[snap[f].w] = snap[f].v
    /\ \A g \in Feeders : snap[f].w \notin holdings[g]
    /\ holdings' = [holdings EXCEPT ![f] = @ \cup {snap[f].w}]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![snap[f].w] = (@ + 1) % (MaxVer + 1)]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![f] = [valid |-> FALSE, w |-> snap[f].w, v |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED retries

\* A read that lost the optimistic race is retried.
Retry(f) ==
    /\ snap[f].valid
    /\ ver[snap[f].w] # snap[f].v
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![f] = [valid |-> FALSE, w |-> snap[f].w, v |-> 0]]
    /\ retries' = IF retries < MaxVer THEN retries + 1 ELSE retries
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holdings, ver>>

\* The feeder finishes shedding and releases the window back to the grid.
Release(f, w) ==
    /\ w \in holdings[f]
    /\ holdings' = [holdings EXCEPT ![f] = @ \ {w}]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![w] = (@ + 1) % (MaxVer + 1)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, retries>>

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Feeders, w \in Windows : ReadWindow(f, w)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Claim(f)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Retry(f)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders, w \in Windows : Release(f, w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No load-shed window is ever allocated to two different feeders at once.
NoDoubleShed ==
    \A f, g \in Feeders :
        f # g => holdings[f] \cap holdings[g] = {}

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Feeders = {f1, f2}
    Windows = {w1, w2}
    MaxVer = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleShed
nl:
A power-grid load shedder assigns time windows during which feeders drop load,
and each shed window may belong to only one feeder at a time. Feeders coordinate
with optimistic locking and retry rather than holding locks. A feeder reads the
version stamp of a window it wants, takes no lock, then attempts to claim it. The
claim succeeds only if the window's version has not moved since the read and no
other feeder currently holds it; concurrent claim requests may be applied in any
order. If the version changed underneath a feeder -- another feeder won the race
-- the read is stale and the feeder retries. When a feeder finishes shedding it
releases the window and bumps its version for the next round. The optimistic
check guarantees two feeders never both hold the same window.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No load-shed window is ever allocated to two different feeders
at the same time.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m3p5t5 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Schedulers, Admin

NONE == "none"

VARIABLES leader, alive, started, startedBy
vars == <<leader, alive, started, startedBy>>

Init ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ alive = [s \in Schedulers |-> TRUE]
    /\ started = FALSE
    /\ startedBy = NONE

\* A live scheduler is elected coordinator when there is no current leader.
Elect(s) ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ alive[s]
    /\ leader' = s
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, started, startedBy>>

\* The leader fails; failover clears the leadership so a new one can be elected.
FailLeader(s) ==
    /\ leader = s
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
    /\ leader' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<started, startedBy>>

\* A previously failed scheduler recovers and may stand for election again.
Recover(s) ==
    /\ ~alive[s]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, started, startedBy>>

\* The irreversible surgery start: only the current leader may fire it, and only
\* if it has not already happened.
StartSurgery(s) ==
    /\ leader = s
    /\ ~started
    /\ started' = TRUE
    /\ startedBy' = s
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive>>

\* Admin override: the chief may force the start regardless of leadership, but
\* still only once.
AdminStart ==
    /\ ~started
    /\ started' = TRUE
    /\ startedBy' = Admin
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Schedulers : Elect(s)
    \/ \E s \in Schedulers : FailLeader(s)
    \/ \E s \in Schedulers : Recover(s)
    \/ \E s \in Schedulers : StartSurgery(s)
    \/ AdminStart

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The irreversible start flag and its recorded initiator agree: the surgery is
\* marked started exactly when some initiator is on record, so it fires at most
\* once and never anonymously.
StartConsistent == started <=> (startedBy # NONE)

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Schedulers = {s1, s2, s3}
    Admin = chief
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT StartConsistent
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler runs on several scheduling nodes that elect
a single leader to coordinate an operating room. A live scheduler is elected
whenever the leadership is vacant. If the leader fails, failover clears the
leadership so a healthy scheduler can be elected in its place, and a failed node
may later recover and stand again. Starting the surgery is an irreversible act:
only the current leader may fire it, and only if it has not already started, so
it can happen at most once. The chief holds a privileged admin override that can
force the surgery to start even without a sitting leader, but that override is
likewise a one-time act. Whoever initiates the start is recorded, so a started
surgery always has exactly one initiator on record.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The irreversible surgery start happens at most once, always
tied to exactly one recorded initiator.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m0p6t3 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Banks, Authorized, Accounts, MaxVer, MaxClock

VARIABLES ver, committed, snap, clock
vars == <<ver, committed, snap, clock>>

Init ==
    /\ ver = [a \in Accounts |-> 0]
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ snap = [b \in Banks |-> [valid |-> FALSE, a |-> CHOOSE x \in Accounts : TRUE, v |-> 0]]
    /\ clock = 0

\* A bank optimistically reads an account's settlement version.
ReadAcct(b, a) ==
    /\ ~snap[b].valid
    /\ ver[a] < MaxVer
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![b] = [valid |-> TRUE, a |-> a, v |-> ver[a]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, committed, clock>>

\* Settle commits only if the bank is authorized and its read is still live.
Settle(b) ==
    /\ b \in Authorized
    /\ snap[b].valid
    /\ ver[snap[b].a] = snap[b].v
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![snap[b].a] = @ + 1]
    /\ committed' = committed \cup { [bank |-> b, acct |-> snap[b].a, ver |-> snap[b].v] }
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![b] = [valid |-> FALSE, a |-> snap[b].a, v |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

\* An unauthorized bank, or one whose read went stale, cannot settle; its
\* pending read is dropped so it must start over.
DropAttempt(b) ==
    /\ snap[b].valid
    /\ (b \notin Authorized \/ ver[snap[b].a] # snap[b].v)
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![b] = [valid |-> FALSE, a |-> snap[b].a, v |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, committed, clock>>

\* Time advances; a slow but live bank simply settles on a later tick.
Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, committed, snap>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ clock = MaxClock
    /\ \A a \in Accounts : ver[a] = MaxVer
    /\ \A b \in Banks : ~snap[b].valid
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Banks, a \in Accounts : ReadAcct(b, a)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Settle(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : DropAttempt(b)
    \/ Tick
    \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every committed settlement was written by a bank on the authorized list.
SettlementsAuthorized == \A r \in committed : r.bank \in Authorized

=============================================================================
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch settles account entries through an optimistic
locking scheme with retry. A bank optimistically reads the settlement version of
an account, taking no lock. It may then commit a settlement, but the commit
succeeds only if the bank is on the authorized settlement list and the version it
read is still live, meaning no one has settled that account in the meantime. A
bank that is not authorized, or whose read has gone stale, cannot commit; its
pending read is discarded and it must start over. Banks can be slow but are
assumed not to have failed, so a settlement clock advances and a lagging bank
simply commits on a later tick. Unauthorized banks and banks acting on stale
reads never leave a committed settlement behind.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every committed settlement was written by a bank on the
authorized settlement list.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m9p1t2 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Instances, Keys, MaxOps

VARIABLES stock, epoch, appliedTo, snap
vars == <<stock, epoch, appliedTo, snap>>

Init ==
    /\ stock = [k \in Keys |-> 0]                        \* shared inventory record
    /\ epoch = 0                                          \* reconfiguration epoch
    /\ appliedTo = [k \in Keys |-> 0]                     \* commits applied per key
    /\ snap = [i \in Instances |-> [valid |-> FALSE, k |-> CHOOSE x \in Keys : TRUE, v |-> 0, e |-> 0]]

\* An instance reads a key's stock together with the current epoch.
Read(i, k) ==
    /\ ~snap[i].valid
    /\ epoch < MaxOps
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![i] = [valid |-> TRUE, k |-> k, v |-> stock[k], e |-> epoch]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, epoch, appliedTo>>

\* Commit the read-modify-write only if the snapshot epoch is still live; this
\* epoch check stops one instance's update from clobbering the other's.
Commit(i) ==
    /\ snap[i].valid
    /\ snap[i].e = epoch
    /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![snap[i].k] = snap[i].v + 1]
    /\ appliedTo' = [appliedTo EXCEPT ![snap[i].k] = @ + 1]
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![i] = [valid |-> FALSE, k |-> snap[i].k, v |-> 0, e |-> 0]]

\* A read stranded on an old epoch is discarded and retried.
Retry(i) ==
    /\ snap[i].valid
    /\ snap[i].e # epoch
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![i] = [valid |-> FALSE, k |-> snap[i].k, v |-> 0, e |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, epoch, appliedTo>>

\* An operator reconfiguration bumps the epoch, invalidating in-flight reads.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxOps
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, appliedTo, snap>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ epoch = MaxOps
    /\ \A i \in Instances : ~snap[i].valid
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances, k \in Keys : Read(i, k)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Commit(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Retry(i)
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No committed update is lost: for every key the stored stock equals the number
\* of commits applied to it, so no instance's write overwrote another's.
NoLostUpdate == \A k \in Keys : stock[k] = appliedTo[k]

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Instances = {east, west}
    Keys = {k1, k2}
    MaxOps = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet is served by two independent controller instances that
share one inventory record, keyed by storage bin, under an epoch-numbered
reconfiguration scheme. Each instance updates a bin with a read-modify-write: it
reads the bin's stock together with the current epoch into a private snapshot,
then tries to commit an incremented value. The commit is accepted only if the
snapshot's epoch still matches the live epoch, an optimistic check that stops one
instance from clobbering the other's committed update. A read stranded on a stale
epoch is discarded and retried. An operator may reconfigure the fleet, bumping
the epoch and invalidating any in-flight reads. Both instances draw from the same
shared record, yet no committed update is ever lost.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every storage bin, the stored stock equals the number of
committed updates applied to it -- no update is lost.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m5p0t1 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Techs, Fridges, Staff, Quorum

NONE == "none"

VARIABLES pos, approvals
vars == <<pos, approvals>>

Init ==
    /\ pos = [t \in Techs |-> NONE]
    /\ approvals = [t \in Techs |-> {}]

\* A staff member approves a technician's request for exclusive fridge access.
\* Approvals accumulate in any order.
Approve(m, t) ==
    /\ m \notin approvals[t]
    /\ pos[t] = NONE
    /\ approvals' = [approvals EXCEPT ![t] = @ \cup {m}]
    /\ UNCHANGED pos

\* A staff member rescinds a pending approval before the technician enters.
Rescind(m, t) ==
    /\ m \in approvals[t]
    /\ approvals' = [approvals EXCEPT ![t] = @ \ {m}]
    /\ UNCHANGED pos

\* A technician takes exclusive control of a cold-storage fridge only after a
\* quorum of staff has approved and no other technician holds that fridge.
Enter(t, fr) ==
    /\ pos[t] = NONE
    /\ Cardinality(approvals[t]) >= Quorum
    /\ \A u \in Techs : pos[u] # fr
    /\ pos' = [pos EXCEPT ![t] = fr]
    /\ approvals' = [approvals EXCEPT ![t] = {}]

\* The technician relinquishes the fridge for the next requester.
Leave(t) ==
    /\ pos[t] # NONE
    /\ pos' = [pos EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED approvals

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Staff, t \in Techs : Approve(m, t)
    \/ \E m \in Staff, t \in Techs : Rescind(m, t)
    \/ \E t \in Techs, fr \in Fridges : Enter(t, fr)
    \/ \E t \in Techs : Leave(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No two distinct technicians ever hold the same cold-storage fridge at once.
FridgeExclusive ==
    \A t, u \in Techs :
        (t # u /\ pos[t] # NONE) => pos[t] # pos[u]

=============================================================================
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker guards its cold-storage fridges as critical
resources: at most one technician may have exclusive control of a given fridge at
a time. Granting that control is not unilateral -- it requires quorum voting by
the bank's staff. A staff member approves a technician's access request, and
because approvals arrive independently they may accumulate in any order; a staff
member may also rescind a pending approval before the technician enters. A
technician takes exclusive control of a fridge only after a quorum of approvals
has gathered and no other technician currently holds that fridge. When finished,
the technician relinquishes the fridge so the next requester may take it. The
quorum-then-exclusive-check discipline keeps two technicians from ever sharing a
fridge.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct technicians ever hold the same cold-storage
fridge at the same time.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m1p6t3 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, MaxEpoch, MaxClock

VARIABLES token, epoch, clearances, clock
vars == <<token, epoch, clearances, clock>>

Init ==
    /\ token = CHOOSE c \in Controllers : TRUE
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ clearances = {}
    /\ clock = 0

\* Exclusive issuing authority is handed to another controller on the ring.
PassToken(c) ==
    /\ c # token
    /\ token' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, clearances, clock>>

\* A handover epoch bump ages out any authority a controller thinks it still has.
BumpEpoch ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, clearances, clock>>

\* A controller issues a takeoff clearance. Only the current token holder is
\* authorized to do so; the issue is recorded with the holder it observed.
Issue(c) ==
    /\ token = c
    /\ clearances' = clearances \cup { [issuer |-> c, holder |-> token] }
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, epoch, clock>>

\* Time advances; a slow but live controller simply issues on a later tick.
Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, epoch, clearances>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : PassToken(c)
    \/ BumpEpoch
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Issue(c)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every clearance was issued by the controller that held the ring token at the
\* moment of issue -- no unauthorized, non-holding controller ever issued one.
ClearancesByHolder ==
    \A r \in clearances : r.issuer = r.holder

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {ctA, ctB, ctC}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    MaxClock = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ClearancesByHolder
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator grants exclusive authority to issue takeoff
clearances using a token ring among the tower controllers. A single token
circulates, and only the controller currently holding it may issue a clearance,
which gives it exclusive access to the runway. The token is handed from one
controller to the next around the ring. A handover epoch may be bumped to age
out any stale belief a controller holds about its authority. When the token
holder issues a clearance, the issue is recorded together with the holder it
observed at that instant. Controllers can be slow but are assumed not to have
failed, so a clock advances and a lagging holder simply issues on a later tick.
A controller that does not hold the token can never issue a valid clearance.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every issued takeoff clearance was made by the controller that
held the ring token at the moment of issue.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m2p2t1 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Participants, Total

VARIABLES phase, prepared, depot, stock
vars == <<phase, prepared, depot, stock>>

Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ prepared = {}
    /\ depot = Total          \* coins held in the machine's coin vault
    /\ stock = 0              \* coins moved into the dispensed tray

\* The coordinator opens a two-phase transaction to move one coin.
Begin ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ phase' = "preparing"
    /\ prepared' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<depot, stock>>

\* A participant votes to prepare. Votes may arrive in any order; no coin moves
\* during the prepare phase.
Prepare(p) ==
    /\ phase = "preparing"
    /\ p \notin prepared
    /\ prepared' = prepared \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, depot, stock>>

\* Only when every participant has prepared does the coordinator commit,
\* atomically moving exactly one coin from the vault to the tray.
Commit ==
    /\ phase = "preparing"
    /\ prepared = Participants
    /\ depot > 0
    /\ depot' = depot - 1
    /\ stock' = stock + 1
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ prepared' = {}

\* If the transaction cannot complete it aborts, and no coin has moved.
Abort ==
    /\ phase = "preparing"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ prepared' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<depot, stock>>

\* A dispensed coin is collected, returning it to the vault for the next sale.
Collect ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ stock > 0
    /\ stock' = stock - 1
    /\ depot' = depot + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, prepared>>

Next ==
    \/ Begin
    \/ \E p \in Participants : Prepare(p)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ Collect

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Coins are conserved: the vault plus the tray always hold the fixed total, so
\* the two-phase protocol neither mints nor loses a coin.
CoinsConserved == depot + stock = Total

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Participants = {p1, p2}
    Total = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CoinsConserved
nl:
A vending machine network moves coins between an internal vault and a dispensed
tray using a two-phase commit across its participant subsystems. A coordinator
opens a transaction to move one coin, entering a prepare phase. Each participant
then votes to prepare, and because these votes arrive independently they may be
recorded in any order; crucially, no coin moves during the prepare phase. Only
once every participant has prepared does the coordinator commit, atomically
moving exactly one coin from the vault to the tray. If the transaction cannot
complete it aborts, leaving every coin where it was. A dispensed coin may later
be collected back into the vault for the next sale. Because value moves only on
an all-prepared commit and always one coin at a time, coins are never created or
destroyed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The vault balance plus the tray balance always equals the fixed
total number of coins.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m1p4t4 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Printers, MaxCap

VARIABLES token, queueLen, cap, active
vars == <<token, queueLen, cap, active>>

Init ==
    /\ token = CHOOSE p \in Printers : TRUE
    /\ queueLen = 0
    /\ cap = MaxCap
    /\ active = TRUE

\* Exclusive submit rights pass to another printer around the ring.
PassToken(p) ==
    /\ p # token
    /\ token' = p
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queueLen, cap, active>>

\* Only the token-holding printer may enqueue a job, and only when the spool is
\* active and the bounded queue has room -- otherwise backpressure blocks it.
Enqueue(p) ==
    /\ token = p
    /\ active
    /\ queueLen < cap
    /\ queueLen' = queueLen + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, cap, active>>

\* A queued job is printed, freeing a slot.
Dequeue ==
    /\ queueLen > 0
    /\ queueLen' = queueLen - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, cap, active>>

\* Operators resize the spool capacity at runtime, but never below the current
\* backlog.
Resize(k) ==
    /\ k \in 0 .. MaxCap
    /\ k >= queueLen
    /\ cap' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, queueLen, active>>

\* The spool is paused or resumed.
Toggle ==
    /\ active' = ~active
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, queueLen, cap>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Printers : PassToken(p)
    \/ \E p \in Printers : Enqueue(p)
    \/ Dequeue
    \/ \E k \in 0 .. MaxCap : Resize(k)
    \/ Toggle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The number of queued jobs never exceeds the current spool capacity.
WithinCapacity == queueLen <= cap

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Printers = {pr1, pr2, pr3}
    MaxCap = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT WithinCapacity
nl:
A print shop job spooler shares submit rights across several printers using a
token ring: a single token circulates, and only the printer currently holding it
may enqueue jobs, giving it exclusive access to the spool. The spool's work queue
is bounded, so the token holder may enqueue a job only when the spool is active
and the queue is below capacity; when the queue is full the spool exerts
backpressure and refuses the job. Queued jobs are printed one at a time, freeing
slots. Operators may resize the spool capacity at runtime to tune throughput, but
never below the jobs already queued. The spool may also be paused and resumed.
Regardless of how capacity is retuned, the backlog is never allowed to overflow
the current capacity.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of queued jobs never exceeds the current spool
capacity.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m4p4t0 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Feeders, ReqIds, Cap, MaxDelivered

VARIABLES queue, crashed, delivered, online
vars == <<queue, crashed, delivered, online>>

Init ==
    /\ queue = {}                              \* the bounded shed-command work queue
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ delivered = 0
    /\ online = [f \in Feeders |-> TRUE]

\* A live, online feeder submits a shed command, but only if the bounded queue
\* has room; a full queue applies backpressure and rejects the submission.
Submit(f, id) ==
    /\ f \notin crashed
    /\ online[f]
    /\ Cardinality(queue) < Cap
    /\ <<f, id>> \notin queue
    /\ queue' = queue \cup { <<f, id>> }
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, delivered, online>>

\* The controller dispatches an arbitrary queued shed command.
Dispatch(req) ==
    /\ req \in queue
    /\ queue' = queue \ {req}
    /\ delivered' = IF delivered < MaxDelivered THEN delivered + 1 ELSE delivered
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, online>>

\* A single feeder may crash silently and then submits nothing further.
Crash(f) ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ crashed' = {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, delivered, online>>

\* A live feeder goes offline or comes back online.
ToggleOnline(f) ==
    /\ f \notin crashed
    /\ online' = [online EXCEPT ![f] = ~@]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, crashed, delivered>>

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Feeders, id \in ReqIds : Submit(f, id)
    \/ \E req \in Feeders \X ReqIds : Dispatch(req)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Crash(f)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : ToggleOnline(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The bounded shed-command queue never holds more commands than its capacity.
QueueBounded == Cardinality(queue) <= Cap

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Feeders = {f1, f2}
    ReqIds = {i1, i2}
    Cap = 2
    MaxDelivered = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT QueueBounded
nl:
A power-grid load shedder collects shed commands from its feeders into a bounded
work queue before a central controller dispatches them. A feeder that is live and
online may submit a shed command, but only when the queue is below its capacity;
when the queue is full it applies backpressure and rejects further submissions.
The controller dispatches queued commands one at a time, and because commands are
held without ordering it may pick any queued command to dispatch next. Any single
feeder may crash silently and thereafter submits nothing further, while healthy
feeders may go offline and come back online as conditions change. No matter how
submissions and dispatches interleave, the number of shed commands buffered in
the queue never exceeds its fixed capacity.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The bounded shed-command queue never holds more commands than
its fixed capacity.
